messages.author: 2a7a9b1c134fcf1f
messages.subject: Re: traceback in errors
parts:
Looks like a few people have run into this issue too.
The alternative proposed here: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2004-March/047653.html seems to catch errors successfully (although I found it somewhat useful to modify try myTry logic to cat the traceback rather than return it).

myTry <- function(expr) {
  withRestarts(
    withCallingHandlers(expr,
                        error = function(e) {
                          error  = e
                          calls  = sys.calls()
                          frames = sys.frames()
                          invokeRestart("myAbort", e, calls, frames)
                        }),
    myAbort = function(e, calls, frames){
      err = list(error = e, calls=calls, frames=frames)
      cat(as.character(err$error), '\n')
      lapply(err$calls, function(x) cat(as.character(x), '\n', file = stderr() ))
      stop()
    }
  )
}

## Example of use
f <- function(x) x + 2
g <- function(...) f(...)
myTry({g(2)})
# Returns 4

myTry({g('dog')})
# Prints the call stack, although it'd probably make sense to filter out the less readable levels, like withRestarts, etc.

messages.author: 7fbb1ca565764061
messages.subject: Re: traceback in errors
parts:
Hi,

I just wanted to ask whether meanwhile there are any updates or solutions to showing informative tracebacks when an error has occured.

While shiny is great, I find debugging complex shiny quite painful because it is so hard to figure out in which function an error has occured.

For example: I get an error message like

Warning: Unhandled error in observer: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
observe({
    if (hasButtonCounterIncreased("GreenParadoxQuiz_CollRunBtn",

But the error has actually occured in some function that was called before, but I have no clue in which function. Using

options(shiny.error=traceback)

does not help, since the traceback does not show the function in which the error has occured.

If it is not possible to implement an informative traceback within a tryCatch, maybe an alternative would be a shiny option to not catch any errors so that the app directly terminates in the function where the error has occured and normal R debugging facilities can be effectively used.

Best wishes,
Sebastian
